derivation: PagerBegin sets dbOrigSize to zero from the empty destination. Backup holds this single destination write transaction across all backup_step calls. Positive page numbers cannot satisfy pgno<=dbOrigSize, so no old-page rollback records are written. There are no savepoints or SQL statements on the destination, hence no statement journal, sort temporary file or super-journal.

pager_open_journal writes one initial sector-sized header. The first cache spill may call syncJournal(newHdr=1), append one more sector header and set state WRITER_DBMOD while clearing all NEED_SYNC page flags. Later new-page writes in that state do not set NEED_SYNC; later spills cannot append another header. Large-sector propagation only propagates existing flags; it cannot originate a flag after the first sync. Backup uses pager writes, not pager page moves.

Commit calls syncJournal(newHdr=0), never appends a third header; its super-journal argument is null. Failure ends this transaction through rollback and has no retry. Sector size is clamped to MAX_SECTOR_SIZE=65536. Thus two headers reserve 131072 bytes even when the VFS uses smaller sectors or keeps the journal in memory.

Destination page size is set to source size before the write transaction. Expected main content plus the full 131072-byte journal and both files entry/inode allowances must fit the already held cli-backup 25 percent envelope BEFORE tmp directory/container creation. No success is returned with an internal sidecar.

These are source-derived byte bounds and declared entry allowances. Local progress observations are samples, not continuous filesystem measurements or production proof. Other application, daemon, unit journal and physical metadata closure remains separate.
preconditions: Exact qualified acc158 image and all four dependency source bytes plus native sqlite_source_id()/sqlite_version() are required.

Output main and journal/WAL/SHM names are absent before source open. Main is exclusively precreated at zero bytes, regular, one link, held by descriptor through backup; owned output directory has one writer.
Native backup.cpp opens its own fresh destination handle, only main, default rollback mode; no attached database, SQL statement, savepoint, extension, URI or custom VFS is used on that handle.
Source has an established read transaction before page_count/page_size and backup; main length is pinned. No installer or production journal setting is changed.
sourceVerification: Fetched primary npm tarball in memory, checked full SHA512 against actual be837974 package-lock integrity, checked all four listed files byte-for-byte against local installed package; no package install/build/host operation.

/*
** The maximum allowed sector size. 64KiB. If the xSectorsize() method
** returns a value larger than this, then MAX_SECTOR_SIZE is used instead.
** This could conceivably cause corruption following a power failure on
** such a system. This is currently an undocumented limit.
*/
#define MAX_SECTOR_SIZE 0x10000

** Pager.journalOff variable by JOURNAL_HDR_SZ so that the next
  ** record is written to the following sector (leaving a gap in the file
  ** that will be implicitly filled in by the OS).
  **
  ** However it has been discovered that on some systems this pattern can
  ** be significantly slower than contiguously writing data to the file,
  ** even if that means explicitly writing data to the block of
  ** (JOURNAL_HDR_SZ - 28) bytes that will not be used. So that is what
  ** is done.
  **
  ** The loop is required here in case the sector-size is larger than the
  ** database page size. Since the zHeader buffer is only Pager.pageSize
  ** bytes in size, more than one call to sqlite3OsWrite() may be required
  ** to populate the entire journal header sector.
  */
  for(nWrite=0; rc==SQLITE_OK&&nWrite<JOURNAL_HDR_SZ(pPager); nWrite+=nHeader){
    IOTRACE(("JHDR %p %lld %d\n", pPager, pPager->journalHdr, nHeader))
    rc = sqlite3OsWrite(pPager->jfd, zHeader, nHeader, pPager->journalOff);
    assert( pPager->journalHdr <= pPager->journalOff );
    pPager->journalOff += nHeader;
  }

  return rc;

/* If a transaction is still open on the Btree, roll it back. */
